name: Unknown male (brought in by ambulance)
presenting_complaint: Found drowsy and unresponsive, no history available

medical_history.social: Found collapsed in a public place. No identification confirmed. Estimated age 50s.
medical_history.family: Unknown — no next of kin available

validation_criteria.presenting_scenario: An approximately 55-year-old man is brought in by ambulance, found drowsy in a public place with no history available. GCS is 8, respiratory rate is 8 with pinpoint pupils, and SpO2 91%. No collateral information has arrived with him. This is an undifferentiated reduced-consciousness presentation.
validation_criteria.task: Document your assessment and initial management as the admitting RMO.

subjective: Document that no history is available and that collateral must be actively chased (this is a TASK, not optional)
Sources to pursue: ambulance crew handover, bystanders, wallet/phone/ID, nursing home, GP, family, My Health Record, old hospital notes
Note pinpoint pupils and low respiratory rate suggest possible opioid toxicity
Ask ambulance about scene findings (needles, medication boxes, alcohol, environment)
objective: Airway assessment FIRST; GCS 8 or less means call anaesthetics for airway protection
Full GCS with E/V/M breakdown, pupils (size/reactivity), respiratory pattern
A-to-E: SpO2, capnography, temperature, signs of trauma/head injury, needle marks
Bloods: BGL, VBG (CO2), UEC, LFT, calcium, FBC, CRP, ethanol, paracetamol and salicylate levels; ECG, septic screen, CT brain
assessment: Reduced GCS of undifferentiated cause — likely opioid toxicity given pinpoint pupils and hypoventilation
Work through reversible causes: glucose, opioids, hypoxia, hypercapnia, hypotension
Wider differential: intracranial bleed, stroke, seizure/post-ictal, sepsis, sodium/calcium derangement, uraemia, hepatic encephalopathy, thyroid/adrenal, toxins, hypothermia
plan: Airway first — GCS 8, so call anaesthetics for airway management while continuing assessment (FIRST action)
High-flow oxygen, IV access, cardiac monitor

Quick reversibles in order: check glucose (give IV glucose if low); naloxone 0.1-0.4 mg IV/IM titrated for suspected opioid toxicity with pinpoint pupils and low RR; correct hypoxia and hypercapnia; treat hypotension
Bloods and screens as above; ECG; CT brain once stabilised
Actively chase collateral history: ambulance, family, nursing home, medication list, GP, My Health Record
Empirical treatment for reversible causes while investigating; escalate to ED consultant/ICU
Consider thiamine 100 mg IV before glucose if alcohol/malnutrition suspected

critical_errors: Treating collateral history as optional rather than an active task — failing to chase ambulance/family/nursing home/GP/My Health Record
Failing to secure/assess the airway with GCS 8 (not calling anaesthetics)
Failing to check and treat reversible causes — glucose, naloxone for opioid toxicity, hypercapnia/hypoxia
must_not_miss: Reversible causes actively excluded/treated (hypoglycaemia, opioid toxicity, hypercapnia, hypoxia)
Collateral history pursued as a defined task
